analyst_view.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 points, unbeaten at home in the league) host Angers (17th, 8 points), winless in five and without a goal in their last three. Liam Rosenior's side lean on Lassine Sinayoko, the league's top scorer with nine goals; Ikoné and Sangui are out (counted), while Adama Camara and centre-back Chergui are doubts. Angers (Stéphane Gilli, a former Paris FC coach) miss the suspended Lefort (counted) and Bané Diatta, plus Oumar Pona after falling ill on Mali U23 duty; the newer news is that striker El Ouazzani has returned from injury (Sports Mole), though The Stats Zone still calls him a fitness doubt. Angers are expected to sit deep, and referee Aurélien Petit (2.5 cards a game in four top-flight games) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already add a little for Lefort's absence in Angers' defence. Angers have not scored in three, but El Ouazzani looks back, Paris FC have conceded in each of their last three home games and Sinayoko is in form; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Against a deep, struggling Angers side Paris FC are likely to have long spells of pressure out wide through Kebbal and their wing-backs, which tends to produce corners, so I nudge it up to about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take some off for Petit's lenient start. Gilli facing his former club adds a little edge, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, with Paris FC doing most of the shooting, and they already add a lot for Paris FC's recent shooting and Angers' leaky last six games. Nothing new adds to that, so I stay at 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Sinayoko is in form for Paris FC, while Angers have barely tested goalkeepers lately; El Ouazzani's return helps them a little, but the numbers already see both teams' trends, so I stay at 8.8.
